notes: 20 queries: 10 should trigger (clear multiverse/specification-curve/robustness-to-analytic-choices requests), 10 should NOT trigger (sensitivity analyses in finance, single-subsample checks, coincidental 'universe'/'spec' vocabulary, ridge lambda sweeps, etc.). The near-misses in slots 11-20 are the hard cases.

evals.prompt: I want to test how robust my regression coefficient is to different outlier exclusion rules, covariate choices, and operationalizations of the IV. Can you help me run a multiverse analysis?
I'm worried my effect might just be an artifact of how I set up the analysis. Is there a way to check whether it holds across different reasonable analytic choices?
My advisor wants a specification curve analysis showing how my main finding changes across different model specifications. How do I do that?
Someone asked about researcher degrees of freedom in my study and whether the result would hold if I had made different choices. I want to address this systematically.

I have 5 defensible decisions in my analysis — outlier rule, whether to include age as a covariate, which of two DV measures to use, whether to log-transform, and which subgroup. Can we enumerate all the universes and run them all?
My result might be a garden-of-forking-paths artifact. I want to run the analysis under every reasonable combination of the choices I could have made and plot the distribution.
I want to check vibration of effects — whether my beta changes a lot depending on how I operationalized the key variables. How do I quantify which decisions drive the most variance?
Can you help me run a specification curve? I have three model variants (OLS, robust regression, quantile regression) crossed with two outlier rules and three DV operationalizations.
A reviewer says my finding is contingent on arbitrary analytic choices. I want to show that the result holds across the multiverse of reasonable specifications.
I want to do a Steegen-style multiverse analysis — enumerate the data multiverse and the model multiverse, run everything, and produce the specification curve with joint permutation inference.
I'm building a DCF valuation model. Can you run a sensitivity analysis showing how the NPV changes as I vary the discount rate from 8% to 15% and the terminal growth rate from 1% to 4%?
As a robustness check I ran the same regression on just the female subsample. The effect held (b=0.31, p=0.04). Does that confirm my finding?
My dataset has a column called 'universe' that indicates which Marvel cinematic universe phase each film belongs to. Can you help me use it to group the data for analysis?
Here is my OpenAPI spec for a REST endpoint. Can you review it and suggest improvements to the request/response schema?
I want to sweep lambda from 0.001 to 10 in my ridge regression to see how the regularization path affects the coefficients. Can you help me plot that?
I ran my primary analysis on the full sample and then repeated it on the pre-registered subsample as a sensitivity check. Both p-values were below 0.05. What should I conclude?
My model has a specification with three hidden layers. I want to try a few variants: two layers, three layers, and adding dropout. Which architecture works best?
I need to stress-test my financial model. Can you vary the revenue growth assumptions between 5% and 20% in 5pp increments and show me the resulting EBITDA range?
What is the universe of possible outcomes if I flip three coins? Can you enumerate all 8 combinations?
I checked one alternative model as a robustness check — added a quadratic term — and the main effect was unchanged. Is that sufficient?
